Subject: Security exhibit + SOC 2 / pen-test language (MSA + OF)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two items before we move to legal: (1) the security exhibit language (SOC 2 assertions, audit rights, evidence cadence) that will attach to the MSA, and (2) where pen-test access and timing live in the Order Form vs exhibit.

High-level asks from MedSync:
- Confirm which SOC 2 assertions Redwood will attest to (CC6, CC7, etc.) and whether we can surface the report summary.
- Pen-test: our security team needs a 30-day notice window option and ephemeral staging access for testers; what operational controls do you need?
- Evidence cadence: monthly snapshots vs quarterly bundles? Procurement prefers a regular, machine-readable evidence handoff where possible.

Could you route a draft exhibit and any sample responses? Also cc'ing Bryce from our audit partner — he'll want to review the proposed inspection bands.

Appreciate it,

Sasha Miller
Sr. IT Procurement
MedSync Health

Attachment: medsync-soc2-questionnaire-answers.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Miller <sasha.miller@medsync.com>, procurement@medsync.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + SOC 2 / pen-test language (MSA + OF)

Sasha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and summarizing next steps so we have a shared plan.

Quick answers up front:
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II, Security and Availability scope. We do not publish CC7 (privacy) by default; we can discuss a scoped addendum if MedSync needs it. We can provide a read-only summary report and an ISO-style SOC cover letter under NDA.
- Pen-test access: we support a 14–45 day notice window; standard is 30 days. We require an approved POA (rules of engagement) and ephemeral staging credentials, and will coordinate a test-window with on-call from our infra team.
- Evidence cadence: our typical cadence is quarterly bundles for deliverables but we can provide a monthly machine-readable telemetry extract for specific assertions (e.g., access logs) where contractually permitted.

I attached a first-pass security exhibit that maps assertions to evidence owners and timing. Laura — would you please review the redline markers around inspection rights and the operational carveouts (ephemeral creds, PII minimization)?

Deliverables / owners:
- Draft security exhibit (attached) — Karthik (will iterate with legal)
- SOC 2 summary & sample evidence index — Security Ops (we'll share after NDA)
- Pen-test runbook & staging checklist — Security Eng (Bryce if you want to validate)

Sasha / Bryce, expect a legal redline from Laura by EOD Monday. If procurement needs the 30-day window as a hard requirement (instead of optional), flag it and we'll escalate with Sales.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sasha Miller <sasha.miller@medsync.com>, procurement@medsync.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + SOC 2 / pen-test language (MSA + OF)

Karthik — I reviewed the draft and added inline comments. Highlights for the thread so procurement has visibility: 

1) Inspection / audit rights (Section 4):
- We can offer an audit rights clause limited to SOC 2 scope with 30-day notice and a mutually agreed timeframe. We prefer a \"documentation-only\" inspection by default; on-site or interactive inspections will require a confined, scheduled window and an NDA amendment.
- Proposed language: \"Customer may request access to audit artifacts and a SOC 2 summary. Full operational access or live forensic exercises require a separate, timeboxed inspection engagement and a written backstop (i.e., order form addendum).\"

2) Pen-test (Section 6):
- Operational controls: require ROE (rules of engagement), a designated Redwood point of contact, and either ephemeral staging creds or scoped IP/rate limits. We will not allow testing against production systems.
- Suggested fallback: if Customer requires production-facing pen-tests, we offer a red-team-as-a-service coordination model (third-party managed window).

3) Evidence cadence & format (Section 3):
- Quarterly bundled evidence is the default. For monthly telemetry, we can provide a sanitized, machine-readable extract for agreed assertions (e.g., access logs, change-control snapshots) under a documented retention and minimization policy.

4) Limitation & liability cross-checks:
- I inserted a carveout limiting the scope of inspection to exclude raw user content and PII (we'll reference specific data handling clauses).

Requested changes from MedSync (if firm):
- Move the 30-day pen-test notice into the Order Form as an option (so customers can choose 30/45-day windows with pricing impact).
- If MedSync needs CC7 coverage, Legal needs a clear business justification and will route to Privacy for review (timeline ~2–3 weeks).

Sasha, please confirm: is procurement willing to accept \"documentation-only\" inspection for standard MSA, and reserve expanded inspection in an Order Form addendum? If not, call that out explicitly and we'll mark the clause for escalation to GC.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
